paragraphs.title: Israel Returns to the Service of the Lord

easy.explanation: The men of Kirjath-jearim brought the ark into the house of Abinadab.
easy.q: Where was the ark of the Lord brought?

easy.explanation: Eleazar, Abinadab's son, was sanctified to keep the ark.
easy.q: Who was sanctified to keep the ark of the Lord?

easy.explanation: The people fasted and said, "We have sinned against the Lord."
easy.q: What did the children of Israel do at Mizpeh?

answers: Put away the strange gods and serve the Lord only
medium.explanation: Samuel told them to put away the strange gods and Ashtaroth and serve the Lord only.
medium.q: What did Samuel tell Israel to do if they returned to the Lord with all their hearts?

answers: So he could pray for them, and they could fast and confess
medium.explanation: Samuel said he would pray for them, and the people gathered, fasted, and confessed.
medium.q: Why did Samuel call the people together at Mizpeh?

answers: They put away Baalim and Ashtaroth
They made an alliance with the Philistines
medium.explanation: The children of Israel put away Baalim and Ashtaroth and served the Lord only.
medium.q: What did the people do after Samuel called them to return to the Lord?

answers: The people moved from personal repentance to public repentance before the Lord
The people abandoned the worship of the Lord
The people prepared to build a palace
challenge.explanation: They first removed false worship and then gathered publicly to fast and confess.
challenge.q: What does the sequence from removing false worship to gathering at Mizpeh show?

answers: To turn Israel back to the Lord so He would deliver them from the Philistines
challenge.explanation: Samuel connected sincere service to the Lord with deliverance from the Philistines.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of the preparation Samuel commanded?

challenge.explanation: The ark had been there twenty years, and then all Israel lamented after the Lord.
challenge.q: Which detail shows how long the ark had remained at Kirjath-jearim before this spiritual renewal?

paragraphs.title: The Confrontation with the Philistines and Samuel's Prayer

easy.explanation: The children of Israel were afraid of the Philistines.
easy.q: How did Israel react when they heard that the Philistines had come against them?

easy.explanation: They asked Samuel to cease not to cry unto the Lord for them.
easy.q: Whom did the people ask to pray for them?

answers: A sucking lamb for a burnt offering
easy.explanation: Samuel took a sucking lamb and offered it wholly as a burnt offering.
easy.q: What did Samuel offer to the Lord?

answers: The Philistines had come against them
There was no room at Mizpeh
medium.explanation: The lords of the Philistines went up against Israel after hearing of the gathering at Mizpeh.
medium.q: Why were the children of Israel afraid?

answers: Cry unto the Lord to save them
Restore the worship of false gods
medium.explanation: They asked Samuel to continue crying unto the Lord for their deliverance.
medium.q: What did Israel ask Samuel to do in their danger?

medium.explanation: The people asked Samuel not to stop crying unto the Lord for them.
medium.q: What does the phrase "Cease not" mean in this passage?

answers: He prayed and offered a burnt offering for Israel
He led the people away from Mizpeh
challenge.explanation: Samuel cried unto the Lord for Israel while offering the lamb as a burnt offering.
challenge.q: How did Samuel respond to the people's request?

answers: Samuel acted on behalf of the whole nation
Samuel acted only for his family
challenge.explanation: The verse says that Samuel cried unto the Lord for Israel.
challenge.q: What does the phrase "for Israel" emphasize?

answers: The Philistines returned home without opposition
challenge.explanation: The passage plainly says, "the Lord heard him."
challenge.q: What happened after Samuel cried unto the Lord?

answers: He thundered upon them and discomfited them
easy.explanation: The Lord thundered with a great thunder and discomfited the Philistines.
easy.q: What did the Lord do to the Philistines?

answers: Built an altar to the Philistines
easy.explanation: The men of Israel pursued the Philistines and smote them.
easy.q: What did the men of Israel do after the Philistines were defeated?

easy.explanation: Samuel called the name of the stone Ebenezer.
easy.q: What name did Samuel give to the stone he set up?

medium.explanation: The Philistines were discomfited and smitten before Israel.
medium.q: What was the result of the Lord's confusion among the Philistines?

medium.explanation: They pursued and smote the Philistines until they came under Bethcar.
medium.q: How far did the Israelites pursue the Philistines?

answers: It marked that the Lord had helped Israel
It was found in Abinadab's house
The Philistines had set it up
medium.explanation: Samuel said, "Hitherto hath the Lord helped us."
medium.q: Why was the stone called Ebenezer?

answers: It marked the beginning of Philistine rule
challenge.explanation: The name Ebenezer commemorated the Lord's help to Israel.
challenge.q: What did setting up the stone after the victory accomplish?

answers: The victory followed Samuel's prayer and the Lord's intervention
The victory came only from the number of soldiers
The victory came from an agreement with the Philistines
challenge.explanation: Samuel prayed, the Lord thundered and confused the Philistines, and Israel pursued them.
challenge.q: What does the order of events show about the source of Israel's victory?

challenge.explanation: Samuel declared that the Lord had helped Israel up to that point.
challenge.q: What does "Hitherto" mean in Samuel's statement?

paragraphs.title: Philistine Submission and the Restoration of the Towns

easy.explanation: The passage says, "So the Philistines were subdued."
easy.q: What happened to the Philistines after Israel's victory?

answers: They were given to the Amorites
easy.explanation: The cities taken by the Philistines were restored to Israel.
easy.q: What happened to the cities the Philistines had taken from Israel?

easy.explanation: The passage says there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.

answers: Come into the coast of Israel
medium.explanation: The Philistines came no more into the coast of Israel.
medium.q: What did the Philistines no longer do during Samuel's days?

answers: Only the building of an altar
The return of cities and the deliverance of the borders from the Philistines
The movement of Israel to Ramah
medium.explanation: The cities were restored, and Israel delivered its coasts from the Philistines.
medium.q: What did the restoration described in these verses include?

medium.explanation: The Philistines were defeated and brought under Israel's control.
medium.q: What does "subdued" mean in this passage?

answers: Their defeat allowed Israel to recover its towns and territory
Their defeat caused Israel to surrender its towns
challenge.explanation: After the Philistines were subdued, the cities they had taken were restored to Israel.
challenge.q: What was the connection between the Philistines being subdued and the restoration of the cities?

answers: The Lord's hand remained against them throughout Samuel's lifetime
The defeat lasted only one day
The defeat began after Samuel died
challenge.explanation: The Lord's hand was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.
challenge.q: What does "all the days of Samuel" indicate about the Philistines' defeat?

answers: Israel moved from conflict and loss to restored territory and peace
Israel moved from peace to war with the Amorites
Israel lost its borders after recovering its cities
challenge.explanation: The Philistines were subdued, the cities were restored, and Israel had peace with the Amorites.
challenge.q: What political change is described in these verses?

answers: All the days of his life
easy.explanation: Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
easy.q: How long did Samuel judge Israel?

easy.explanation: Samuel went in circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpeh.
easy.q: Which places did Samuel visit from year to year?

easy.explanation: Samuel returned to Ramah, for there was his house.

answers: He collected taxes from the Philistines
medium.explanation: Samuel judged Israel in all those places.
medium.q: What did Samuel do in the places where he traveled?

answers: Built an altar unto the Lord
Offered the ark of the Lord
medium.explanation: At Ramah, Samuel built an altar unto the Lord.
medium.q: What did Samuel do at Ramah besides judging Israel?

answers: He traveled from place to place each year
medium.explanation: Samuel traveled among Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpeh each year.
medium.q: What does the phrase "from year to year in circuit" mean?

answers: He combined traveling public service with a permanent home
He judged only from his own house
He moved permanently to every city he visited
challenge.explanation: Samuel judged throughout the land but returned to his home in Ramah.
challenge.q: What does Samuel's traveling and returning to Ramah show about his leadership?

answers: It shows that his leadership also included worship of the Lord
It shows that he stopped judging Israel
It shows that he turned to idolatry
challenge.explanation: Alongside judging Israel, Samuel built an altar unto the Lord.
challenge.q: How does the altar at Ramah relate to Samuel's leadership?

answers: He judged Israel all the days of his life
He judged only during the battle
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes the continuance of Samuel's leadership?
